union.summary: Attacker-controlled range endpoints are never capped, so an expanded unbounded range can enumerate an unbounded number of cells (stored DoS in a collaborative doc)
union.evidence: `resolveRange` only fills *omitted* endpoint parts from `bounds`; explicit parts pass through unclamped: `to: { r: b.r ?? max.r, c: b.c ?? max.c }`. The new grammar `ROW: '$'? [1-9][0-9]*` has no digit-count limit, so `=SUM(1:100000000)` parses, `parsePartialRef` does `parseInt(match[2],10)` with no ceiling, and the resulting Range is handed to `toSrefs` in three newly added paths: calculator.ts (`extractReferences(formula)` → `sheet.fetchGridByReferences`), memory.ts `buildDependantsMap` (`toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds)))`), and yorkie-store.ts:566/585/601 (same, three loops). Even without a huge literal, one populated cell far down the sheet (A1000000) makes `=SUM(A:A)` expand to a million-cell range. Attack: a collaborator writes such a formula into a Yorkie-synced sheet; the formula is persisted and `buildDependantsMap` is rebuilt on *every* edit by *every* client, so every peer hangs/OOMs on each keystroke and again on document reopen. The pre-existing `A1:A100000000` form was equivalent for the evaluator, but the dependants-map expansion path is new in this diff and has no size guard.

union.summary: CellIndex.bounds() can return Infinity/-Infinity coordinates, which flow unvalidated into range expansion and cell enumeration
union.evidence: `bounds()` guards only `this.rowIndex.size === 0`, then computes minC/maxC by iterating `this.colIndex.keys()`. If `colIndex` is empty (or holds stale empty buckets) while `rowIndex` is not — e.g. divergent maintenance of the two indexes after deletions — it returns `[{r:minR,c:Infinity},{r:maxR,c:-Infinity}]`. That Range is passed straight to `expandUnboundedRanges` → `resolveRange` (`c: b.c ?? max.c`) → `toRange` → `toSrng`, producing either a non-terminating column-label conversion or a garbage reference string that is then evaluated (`evaluateWithSpill(formula, grid)` in calculator.ts). No caller validates finiteness. Impact is a client hang triggered by ordinary document state; I could not confirm whether rowIndex/colIndex can actually diverge because the working tree was unavailable.

union.summary: Unbounded-range expansion can amplify spill writes, letting one formula overwrite unrelated cells across the sheet
union.evidence: calculator.ts now evaluates the *expanded* formula: `const result = evaluateWithSpill(formula, grid)` where `formula = expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f!, await sheet.getUsedBounds())`. For array-returning functions the spill region is derived from the result dimensions, so `=SORT(A:A)` (or any spilling function over `A:A` / `1:1`) now produces a spill sized to the sheet's full data extent rather than an author-typed range. In a shared document that means a single cell edit can write over a large block of other users' cells — an integrity/unauthorized-write amplification introduced by the expansion, with no cap on the expanded dimensions. I could not trace the spill-write guard code (working tree unavailable), hence low confidence.

union.summary: Evaluated formula string is reconstructed by token concatenation, so stored/displayed `cell.f` can diverge from what is actually computed
union.evidence: `expandUnboundedRanges` rebuilds the formula as `'=' + body` where `body` is the concatenation of `token.text` from `extractTokens(formula)` (which per the design doc synthesizes STRING tokens to fill gaps). The calculator evaluates this reconstructed string while persisting the original `cell.f`. If reassembly is lossy for any input (whitespace, quoted sheet names, unrecognized text turned into gap tokens), a crafted formula would display one expression to reviewers/collaborators while computing another — a spoofing/trust-boundary weakness rather than a memory-safety one. Also note the `catch {}` at the `toSrng(resolveRange(...))` call silently falls back to the raw text, so malformed endpoints are accepted rather than rejected.

union.summary: New Store.getUsedBounds() exposes the sheet's populated data extent through every store implementation with no access check
union.evidence: `getUsedBounds(): Promise<Range | undefined>` is added to the `Store` interface and implemented unconditionally by MemStore, ReadOnlyStore (readonly.ts:157) and YorkieStore (yorkie-store.ts:614) by delegating to `cellIndex.bounds()`, and re-exposed publicly via `Sheet.getUsedBounds()` (sheet.ts) and the package barrel (`expandUnboundedRanges` in src/index.ts). If any store variant is intended to present a permission-filtered or partially-loaded view of a sheet, bounds() reports min/max row/col over the whole underlying index and would disclose the existence/extent of data outside that view. I could not confirm whether any store is permission-scoped, so this is a hardening note.

union.summary: Unbounded range expansion has no cardinality cap — attacker-controlled formula (or a single far-off cell in a shared doc) expands to an arbitrarily large concrete range, causing CPU/memory exhaustion (DoS)
union.evidence:
Vector A (pure formula, no collaboration needed): the grammar's ROW fragment is `'$'? [1-9][0-9]*` with no magnitude limit (packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4, new `fragment ROW`), and REFRANGE now accepts `ROW ':' ROW`. So `=SUM(1:100000000)` lexes as one REFERENCE token. `expandUnboundedRanges` (packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts, new function) calls `resolveRange(token.text.toUpperCase(), resolved)`, which in coordinates.ts returns `toRange({r:1,c:1},{r:100000000,c:max.c})` — no clamp against the `to` row, only omitted parts are filled from bounds. The resulting concrete Srng flows into `extractReferences` → `sheet.fetchGridByReferences` (calculator.ts) and into `toSrefs([node.v])` in arguments.ts, which enumerates every cell ref in the range — 1e8+ string allocations and Map lookups (the new `grid.get(ref)` blank-skip in arguments.ts adds one lookup per cell). The tab hangs / OOMs.

Vector B (remote amplification, collaborative store): bounds come from `CellIndex.bounds()` = min/max populated row/col. Any collaborator writing one cell at, say, r=1048576/c=16384 makes every existing `=SUM(A:A)` / `=COUNT(A:B)` in the doc expand to a range of up to 1.7e10 cells. Worse, `YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts, three new `expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds)` call sites) and `MemStore.buildDependantsMap` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts) run this expansion for EVERY formula cell and are rebuilt on EVERY edit, inserting one dependants-map entry per enumerated cell — so the cost is (#formulas × range size) per keystroke-commit, plus unbounded Map growth. A remote peer therefore freezes every other client's browser by writing a single cell.

Fix direction: cap the expanded range (max rows/cols, or reject ranges whose cell count exceeds a limit) inside `resolveRange`/`expandUnboundedRanges`, and bound the ROW fragment in the grammar.

union.summary: `resolveRange` / `parsePartialRef` are exported with no length or magnitude validation, so non-lexer callers can produce absurd column indices
union.evidence: `parsePartialRef` matches `/^([A-Za-z]*)([0-9]*)$/` — the letter group is unbounded, unlike the grammar's `COL` fragment which caps at 3 letters. `resolveRange` is exported from coordinates.ts (and reachable via the public surface exercised in coordinates.test.ts), so a caller passing e.g. `'AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA:1'` yields a column index from `parseColumnLabel` far beyond any sheet, and `parseInt` on a long digit run yields a row up to Infinity. Combined with the finding above, the resulting `Range` is enumerated cell-by-cell. Row/column values should be validated against a hard maximum before being returned.

union.summary: Bare `catch {}` in `expandUnboundedRanges` silently swallows all parse failures and falls through to the raw, unexpanded token (fail-open on error)
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts: `try { body += toSrng(resolveRange(token.text.toUpperCase(), resolved)); continue; } catch { /* Fall through to the original text on any parse failure. */ }`. The catch is untyped and catches TypeErrors too — e.g. `resolveRange` does `srng.split(':')` and passes `toStr` (possibly `undefined`) to `parsePartialRef`, which calls `.replace` on it. Any such internal defect is invisibly downgraded to "emit the unexpanded reference", which then reaches the evaluator/dependants map in a shape the rest of the pipeline was explicitly changed to no longer expect. Narrow the catch and surface/log the failure rather than proceeding with untransformed input.

union.summary: Evaluated formula text differs from stored `cell.f`, so what is executed is not what is stored/displayed
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts now evaluates `expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f!, await sheet.getUsedBounds())` while `cell.f` retains the original string. The rewritten string is rebuilt by concatenating `extractTokens` output (`'=' + body`), i.e. a re-serialization round-trip of untrusted input. If token reconstruction ever loses or reorders characters, the executed formula would diverge from the one a reviewer sees in the cell. Not exploitable on its own; worth an invariant test that `expandUnboundedRanges(f, b) === f` for every formula containing no unbounded ref (the diff only spot-checks three).
